audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension is repeatedly described as containing a fear ('a fear in fights', 'area fear-and-drain'), and Nevermove is referred to only as 'Root' with no mention of how it works.
audit.why: Riot's text for Demonic Ascension: Swain transforms, drains health from nearby enemies, and can cast Demonflare for damage and a slow. There is no fear anywhere in the kit — the only crowd control is Nevermove's root and pull. Nevermove (E, 850 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) launches a wave forward that roots on its RETURN trip, after which he can pull rooted champions closer. That return-trip timing is the entire dodge.
audit.corrected: Call it a drain-and-slow ultimate at 650 range on a flat 120s, and teach the Nevermove return wave as the thing to sidestep.
sources: brief enemyKit E and R text

audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer, and the shape is right: Annie owns 3 through first item, Swain takes over at two-plus items as Soul Fragment health and the drain scale.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears once as 'his sustain' with no timing and no source named.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him off Soul Fragments and permanently raises his max health, which is why raw resistances are the wrong answer and Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Name Ravenous Flock and buy Grievous Wounds before the second item.

notes: Swain has no fear in his kit — the page claimed one three times (spikes[1], spikes[3], late). His only hard CC is Nevermove's root, and it roots on the wave's RETURN trip, which is the dodge the page never taught. Demonic Ascension was also described as needing 'melee range'; it is 650, which is further than Annie's Q (625) but reachable, so the advice needed a number rather than a category. dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' for a flat 120s ultimate.
